You write the final report of a trial-autopsy system for an analyst. Plain language, precise,
no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

Return JSON only:
{"headline": "<one sentence verdict>",

 "key_evidence": ["<short bullet with the number and its source title>", "..."],
 "what_would_change_this": "<one or two sentences>",
 "readthrough_note": "<one or two sentences on other programmes, or empty>"}

response: {"headline": "JUPITER trial stopped early on 31 March 2008 with 'unequivocal evidence' of cardiovascular benefit for rosuvastatin 20 mg in primary prevention (hsCRP ≥2 mg/L, LDL-C <130 mg/dL); mechanism prediction (HR 0.70) aligns with observed large effect, but calculator flags 'insufficient_data' due to missing follow-up and event inputs.", "summary": "The JUPITER trial randomized 17,802 participants to rosuvastatin 20 mg or placebo and was halted on 31 March 2008 after a median ~1.9 years because the DSMB found 'unequivocal evidence of a reduction in cardiovascular morbidity and mortality.' The calculator, using a modeled −51% LDL-C reduction from a baseline of 2.8 mmol/L, predicts a hazard ratio of 0.701 (29.9% RRR), consistent with the observed HR ~0.56 for the primary endpoint. LDL-C causality is strongly supported by prior statin trials (WOSCOPS HR 0.76, CARE HR 0.76) and human genetics. The only pre-cutoff HMGCR variant shows a null CHD association, leaving target genetics 'uncertain' at the 2008 cutoff, though clinical validation via multiple statin trials supersedes this gap. Confidence is high given the early stopping for efficacy and large sample size.", "key_evidence": ["Trial stopped early 31 March 2008 with DSMB statement: 'unequivocal evidence of a reduction in cardiovascular morbidity and mortality' (Crestor Outcomes Study JUPITER Closes Early Due To Unequivocal Evidence Of Benefit)", "17,802 participants randomized (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00239681)", "Primary endpoint: Time to Major Cardiac Event up to 5 years (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00239681)", "Calculator predicts HR 0.701 (29.9% RRR) from modeled −51% LDL-C reduction at baseline 2.8 mmol/L (calculator)", "WOSCOPS (pravastatin) HR 0.76 and CARE (pravastatin) HR 0.76 confirm LDL-C lowering translates to CV benefit pre-cutoff (Prevention of coronary heart disease with pravastatin in men with hypercholesterolemia; The effect of pravastatin on coronary events after myocardial infarction)", "CORONA trial (rosuvastatin 10 mg) showed −45% placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction (Rosuvastatin in older patients with systolic heart failure)", "HMGCR genetic association score 0.695 but evidence_before_cutoff=0; pre-cutoff HMGCR i18 T>G variant shows null CHD association (opentargets:HMGCR; Genetic variation at the LDL receptor and HMG-CoA reductase gene loci, lipid levels, statin response, and cardiovascular disease incidence in PROSPER)"], "what_would_change_this": "Published JUPITER primary results with HR, 95% CI, and event counts would confirm the magnitude of benefit and allow direct comparison to the mechanism prediction. Long-term follow-up data on diabetes incidence and cancer would address the caveats from early stopping.", "readthrough_note": "The neutral CORONA trial (heart failure, same drug 10 mg) and later AURORA trial (ESRD on hemodialysis) show LDL-C lowering does not translate to benefit when non-atherosclerotic mechanisms dominate in advanced organ failure, underscoring that JUPITER's success is population-specific."}
